newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel's gold plan criticised by own CSU party.
newsitem.headline: Waigel's gold plan criticised by own CSU party.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel has been criticised by members of his own party, the Bavarian-based Christian Social Union (CSU), over his controversial plans to revalue central bank assets.

CSU party sources on Tuesday confirmed press reports that CSU state premier of Bavaria Edmund Stoiber had called on Waigel, who is CSU party leader, to find a consensus with the Bundesbank which opposes the plan to help stop budget gaps.

CSU leader in the Bavarian regional assembly, Alois Glueck, warned Waigel his plan to revalue gold and currency reserves to help Germany qualify for European monetary union (EMU) could not be done without the consent of the Bundesbank, they said.
Stoiber and Glueck had made these remarks during a meeting of CSU leaders on Monday, the sources said.
Waigel said on Monday he would try to reach agreement with the Bundesbank before proposing legal changes to the Bundesbank law to revalue its assets.

Waigel said the Bundesbank was already in general agreement with the plan, despite the objections it has voiced. The main difference is over whether the revaluation would take effect this year or next, he said.
